extracted.intended_audience: MathML implementers, web developers, browser/renderer authors, and authors of math/content-conversion tools
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative rules for authoring Presentation and Content MathML (element semantics, attributes, rendering expectations, and recommended encodings) to ensure interoperable layout and semantic encoding of mathematical expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: msrow element layout and directionality
rubrics_metrics.description: If an mn element is a child of msrow (implicit or explicit), the number is split into its digits and the digits are placed into successive columns; any other element (except mstyle) is treated as a single digit occupying the next column. The empty element <mrow/> may be used to create an empty column. A row is considered primarily as if it were a number, which is always displayed left-to-right, so the directionality used to display the columns is always left-to-right; textual bidirectionality within token elements (other than mn) and overall directionality within children of the msrow still apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mstyle is treated as if its children were directly children of msrow but with style affected by mstyle attributes. See 3.1.5 Directionality for interplay with bidirectional text.

rubrics_metrics.name: msrow position attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: msrow accepts a position attribute (integer, default 0) specifying the horizontal position of the row within the group relative to the containing msgroup (according to its position and shift attributes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resulting position is relative to the column specified by stackalign of the containing mstack or mlongdiv. Positive values move each row toward the tens digit (padding with empty columns on the right); negative values move toward the ones digit (padding on the left). The decimal point is counted as a column and should be taken into account for negative values.

rubrics_metrics.name: mscarries purpose and placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: mscarries is used for annotations like carries, borrows, and crossouts occurring in elementary math. Its children are associated with elements in the following row of the mstack; it is an error for mscarries to be the last element of an mstack or mlongdiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each child of mscarries applies to the same column in the following row. Attachment of carries to columns proceeds left-to-right regardless of overall directionality (directionality may apply to each carry's contents). Children other than mscarry or <mrow/> are treated as implicitly surrounded by mscarry; use <mrow/> when no carry for a particular column is needed. mscarries sets displaystyle false and increments scriptlevel by 1; it changes the default scriptsizemultiplier (default inside mscarries should be 0.6 unless overridden).

rubrics_metrics.name: mscarries attributes and semantics (position, location, crossout, scriptsizemultiplier)
rubrics_metrics.description: mscarries accepts attributes: position (integer, default 0), location (compass values, default 'n'), crossout (list of strike styles or 'none'), and scriptsizemultiplier (number, inherited default 0.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: position specifies horizontal association relative to containing msgroup and stackalign; location specifies carry placement relative to character below using compass directions; crossout may be one or more of 'updiagonalstrike', 'downdiagonalstrike', 'verticalstrike', 'horizontalstrike' (case-insensitive), 'none' is ignored if combined with others; crossouts apply only for columns with a corresponding mscarry and should be drawn using mathcolor. scriptsizemultiplier may be set to override inherited value.

rubrics_metrics.name: mscarry element semantics and attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: mscarry is used inside mscarries to represent the carry for an individual column and is treated as if its width were zero (it does not affect column width and may extend beyond column boundaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mscarry may override the containing mscarries' location and/or crossout attributes. Using <mrow/> as mscarry content can display no actual carry while still enabling a crossout to be drawn. mscarry accepts location and crossout attributes (inherited by default), with the same compass-direction and crossout-value rules as mscarries (case-insensitive comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: msline element purpose and attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: msline draws a horizontal line inside an mstack. Its position, length, and thickness are specified as attributes. If length is specified, the line is positioned/drawn as if it were a number with that number of digits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes: position (integer, default 0) behaves relative to containing msgroup/stackalign similar to msrow; length (unsigned-integer, default 0) specifies number of columns to span (0 means span all columns, in which case position and stackalign have no effect); leftoverhang/rightoverhang (length, default 0) specify extra overhang on left/right; mslinethickness (length or 'thin'|'medium'|'thick', default 'medium') specifies thickness; the line should be drawn using mathcolor. Note: line should have height=0 and depth=mslinethickness so top of msline is on surrounding baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: use <mrow/> to create empty column
rubrics_metrics.description: The empty element <mrow/> may be used to create an empty column in an mstack/msrow to achieve desired alignment and padding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show using <mrow/> to fill columns under particular digits or operators so that alignment (e.g., operator placed at left or right) appears as intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: operator column treatment and default alignment behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing an operator '+' or '-' alongside a number within an addition or subtraction creates a column for the operator; digits inside mn occupy individual columns. A row is treated as a number and displayed left-to-right; default alignment is on the implied decimal point to the right of the numbers unless stackalign or position/shift adjustments are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate operator placement to left (common) or right (used in some countries). Because default alignment may be on an implied decimal point, explicit padding or position adjustments are not always necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: use mscarries/mscarry and menclose for crossouts and borrow/borrow-annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: mscarries and mscarry are the mechanisms for representing carries/borrows and for drawing crossouts (e.g., diagonal strike) on specific columns; menclose can be used within carries to create underlines/other notations used in some national conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mscarry when crossout should apply to a single column; use <mrow/> inside mscarry to indicate no carry while enabling crossout (via the enclosing mscarries). Crossout styles drawn should use mathcolor.

rubrics_metrics.name: msgroup and shift/position for multi-row layouts (e.g., multiplication)
rubrics_metrics.description: msgroup groups rows in an mstack and msgroup's shift and/or position attributes affect the horizontal placement of its children (useful for multi-row multiplication layouts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied msgroups may not change layout; removing a msgroup may require explicit msrow and position/shift attributes or insertion of <mrow/> to pad digits. Use shift to offset groups like partial products, and use msrow position when needed for last-children alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: mlongdiv longdivstyle and long division layout variability
rubrics_metrics.description: The layout used for long division is controlled by the longdivstyle attribute on mlongdiv; notations vary internationally in divisor position, quotient/remainder/intermediate term placement, and line lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers should support the listed longdivstyle values (e.g., lefttop, stackedrightright, stackedleftlinetop, etc.). Nested msgroups and their position/shift attributes determine precise alignment for intermediate results; examples show aligning on '.' vs using ',' as decimal depending on locale.

rubrics_metrics.name: repeating-decimal notations using mstack/msline and stackalign
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeating decimals (e.g., 1/3 = 0.333...) may be represented by putting a horizontal line over repeating digits (or underline in some locales) or by placing dots over digits. These are encoded using mstack, msrow, msline with appropriate length and stackalign settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate stackalign='right' with msline length set to the number of repeating digits; alternative arrangements include placing msline before/after the mn child or using msrow to position decimal points/dots.

rubrics_metrics.name: maction: binding actions to sub-expressions and event semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: maction provides a mechanism to bind actions to expressions, accepting any number of sub-expressions and controlled by an actiontype attribute (open-ended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes: actiontype (string) specifies what should happen; conforming renderers may ignore unknown values. selection (positive-integer, default 1) selects which child is viewed; selection must be 1..number_of_children or it's an error. If actiontype unsupported or absent, render the selected sub-expression. When copying MathML to clipboard, maction elements should be given selection values corresponding to selection state at copy time. For nested maction elements receiving the same event, the innermost maction of each action type should respond. maction is not for linking; non-standard data-* attributes may be used to pass extra info to renderers.

rubrics_metrics.name: semantics element: semantic annotations must be processed
rubrics_metrics.description: The semantics element allows specifying semantic annotations to presentation MathML elements (these annotations may be content MathML or other notations); semantics is part of both presentation and content MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All MathML processors should process the semantics element even if they only process presentation or only content. A presentation MathML expression is typically the first child of semantics, or can be inside annotation-xml with encoding='application/mathml-presentation+xml' (renderers should use that value). See chapter on annotating MathML for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: purpose of Content MathML: encode mathematical meaning not notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Content Markup's purpose is to provide an explicit encoding of the underlying mathematical meaning of an expression rather than any particular notation, because mathematical notation can be ambiguous or vary by community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content MathML enables interchange between semantic processors (CAS, theorem provers, translation systems, automated scoring, search, interactive textbooks). It presents a rigorous extensible framework: Strict Content MathML for uniform structure, full Content MathML for backward compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: content expression primitives and structure (cn, ci, csymbol, apply, bind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content MathML represents expressions as trees built from basic building blocks: numbers (cn), identifiers (ci), symbols (csymbol), function application (apply), and binding (bind).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal nodes represent numbers/variables/symbols; internal nodes represent applications or binding constructions. apply groups the function with its arguments; bind with bvar is used for binding operators. Use these elements to express mathematical structure independent of presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: variable binding: strict vs non-strict usage
rubrics_metrics.description: In Strict Content MathML, the only way to perform variable binding is using bind with bvar. In non-Strict Content markup other idiomatic constructs (qualifier elements) may implicitly bind variables (e.g., limit-style sum/integral notation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bound variables may be renamed consistently within scope without changing meaning. Expressions with qualifiers follow idiomatic patterns; see operator classes (e.g., sums and products share index-variable patterns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict Content MathML design and OpenMath mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Strict Content MathML (introduced in MathML 3) is a minimal subset sufficient to represent meaning using a uniform structure: csymbol for functions, apply/bind for composition, and token elements (cn, ci) with restricted attributes and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict Content MathML is compatible with OpenMath (mapping table provided). The formal semantics are given by specifying equivalent Strict Content MathML expressions and transformation rules (The Strict Content MathML Transformation, Appendix F). Conformant processors need not implement the transformation algorithm and may render equivalent expressions differently; Content MathML does not normatively define computational behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: content dictionaries and csymbol semantics (informative vs normative)
rubrics_metrics.description: csymbol references a Content Dictionary to describe the mathematical semantics of a symbol. The correspondence between Content MathML operator elements and Content Dictionary definitions is provided (informatively) by references to OpenMath content dictionaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The semantic definitions in OpenMath Content Dictionaries are informative, not normative; precise semantics for high-precision contexts are the responsibility of the relevant community, which should verify, extend or replace OpenMath definitions as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: cn element: types, base, and rendering rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The cn element represents numbers. In Strict Content MathML the type attribute is mandatory and may be 'integer', 'real', 'double', or 'hexdouble' (default is real in non-Strict). The base attribute (default 10) indicates digit base for integer/real and is allowed in non-Strict for different encodings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict types: integer = optional sign + digits; real = radix notation with optional sign and decimal point; double = IEEE 754 double lexical forms (e.g., -1E4, INF); hexdouble = 16 hex digits representing IEEE 754 bits. Default rendering of cn text content is same as Presentation mn with suggested variants when attributes/sep used. Non-Strict supports additional types (e-notation, rational, complex-*), use <sep/> for e-notation and separated parts. For base>10 letters A-Z/a-z used as digits (case-insensitive). When base>36 additional digit characters are application-specific.
